chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who marries a virgin for temporary marriage (Mut'ah), he said: It is disliked due to the defect (impurity) upon her family.

key_terms.لِلْعَيْبِ: Due to the defect/impurity, referring to the loss of virginity which is a 'defect' in the bride's value relative to her family.
key_terms.مُتْعَةً: Temporary marriage (Mut'ah), a form of marriage with a specified duration and dowry.
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: Disliked (Makruh), a juristic ruling indicating it is recommended to avoid but not forbidden.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a virgin in temporary marriage according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar highlights a specific juristic nuance in Shia fiqh regarding temporary marriage (Mut'ah), where marrying a virgin is deemed makruh (disliked) due to the economic disadvantage imposed on her family. Unlike permanent marriage, where the husband typically compensates the family for the 'value' of virginity, the shorter duration of Mut'ah may not fully offset this loss, making it less preferable for the bride's kin.
